items.title: October U.S. existing-home sales plunge 5.5% to 16-year low amid elevated mortgage rates
items.summary: The National Association of Realtors reported a 5.5% monthly fall in October existing-home sales to a 3.75 million seasonally adjusted annual rate, the weakest since August 2010. The decline underscores interest-rate pressure on housing transactions, even as median prices held higher year over year. Housing-related stocks are watch indicators; no company-share price change is attributed to this release.

observations.label: Official release, November 12 at 10:00 AM EST
observations.value: October existing-home sales -5.5% month over month, -8.8% year over year, at 3.75 million seasonally adjusted annual rate; lowest since August 2010

observations.label: Inventory and price
observations.value: 1.59 million existing homes available, 5.1 months supply; median sale price $416,700, +0.4% year over year

observations.label: Mortgage/rate context
observations.value: NAR cites 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaging 7.33% in October, versus 6.86% in September; higher financing cost weighs on turnover

observations.label: Market confirmation boundary
observations.value: Data confirmed by original NAR release and independent AP/WSJ coverage. No verified intraday XHB, ITB or Z move linked to the report; those tickers are exposure watch indicators, not asserted movers

observations.label: Watch/invalidation
observations.value: October pending-home-sales release November 18, weekly mortgage-rate trend, housing inventory, regional sales, affordability, housing-linked earnings, 10-year Treasury yields; a sustained mortgage-rate decline with pending-sales recovery would soften the concern

items.key_finding: Housing transaction volume reached a 16-year low, a verified macro deterioration that amplifies sensitivity to high rates.

sources.title: National Association of Realtors, November 12 existing-home sales report
Associated Press, November 12 housing market report
Wall Street Journal, November 12 existing-home sales

items.title: EIA reports surprise 4.7 million-barrel U.S. crude build as oil remains geopolitical
items.summary: The EIA reported U.S. commercial crude inventories rising 4.7 million barrels in the week ended November 6, versus market expectations for a roughly 0.6–0.7 million-barrel draw. Gasoline and distillate stocks also increased. Domestic stock growth argues against a uniformly tight U.S. supply picture, even while the Hormuz security premium remains influential.

observations.label: EIA release, November 12 at noon ET; week ended November 6
observations.value: Commercial crude +4.7 million barrels to 414.4 million; approximately 4% below seasonal five-year average

observations.label: Expectation and surprise
observations.value: Consensus near -0.6 million barrels (Investing.com) to -0.7 million (WSJ); actual build roughly 5.3–5.4 million barrels above expected change

observations.label: Refined product inventories
observations.value: Gasoline +1.8 million barrels; distillates +4.1 million; total commercial petroleum inventories +11.4 million barrels

observations.label: Physical drivers
observations.value: Imports +325,000 barrels/day to 6.7 million; refinery utilization 95.2%; average refinery inputs 17.0 million barrels/day

observations.label: Context, not a verified causal claim
observations.value: AP observed Brent $94.47 (+1.8%) at 12:46 PM ET following U.S.-Iran diplomatic comments; oil reaction to inventories alone is not established

observations.label: Next evidence / invalidation
observations.value: Watch ensuing EIA export/import changes, gasoline and distillate demand, crude price settlement on independently confirmed feeds, XLE/XOP breadth, UKMTO/MARAD ship advisories and verified Hormuz transit

items.key_finding: An official large U.S. inventory build complicates the supply-tightness narrative despite persistent geopolitical oil risk.

sources.title: U.S. EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report summary, released November 12, 2026
Wall Street Journal, U.S. Crude-Oil Stockpiles Post Unexpected Weekly Build, November 12
Associated Press, November 12 midday market and Brent oil reaction

items.title: Indian shipping minister confirms separate November 11 tanker strike off UAE
items.summary: India's shipping minister confirmed that the Liberia-flagged crude tanker MT Dominica Prosperity was struck while drifting off Mina Saqr on November 11. UAE Coast Guard evacuated its entire crew without injuries. This adds specific physical maritime-security evidence, but neither the attacker's identity nor a new export-volume interruption has been established.

observations.label: Physical incident, November 11; minister confirmation November 12
observations.value: MT Dominica Prosperity targeted by projectile off Mina Saqr, UAE; 22 crew evacuated, including 19 Indian nationals; no injuries reported

observations.label: Distinction from previous incidents
observations.value: Separate from November 10 MT Fujairah Energy strike, where four crew were injured; officials had also monitored a possible November 11 NCC Fajr incident

observations.label: Market context, November 12 late morning
observations.value: AP reported Brent near $93.89 (+1.2%) after moving from about $92 to above $94 on US-Iran diplomacy comments; intraday, not settlement

observations.label: Evidence limits
observations.value: Incident confirmed in Indian minister's statement; attacker, damage, export volume affected and latest AIS status not independently established

observations.label: Next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: New UKMTO warnings, MARAD 2026-011 and 2026-013, verified Gulf transit/export counts, freight and war-risk premiums, EIA weekly report and physical vessel status

items.key_finding: Another specifically identified tanker strike reinforces maritime risk, without proof of an incremental oil export shutdown.

sources.title: Press Trust of India, November 12 report carried by Rediff
Times of India, November 12, shipping minister confirmation

items.title: AMD and Broadcom become S&P 500 leaders as Nvidia recovers from opening plunge
items.summary: Late-morning trading showed AMD and Broadcom leading the S&P 500 while Nvidia remained lower following its confirmed leadership change. The dispersion supports a provisional rotation toward competing AI silicon rather than a uniformly weaker AI sector. The relative performance is intraday and could reverse before the close.

observations.label: Late morning November 12, FactSet data cited by MarketWatch
observations.value: AMD +7.4%, AVGO +7.1%, NVDA down more than 4%; intraday indications, not settlement or closing prices

observations.label: AP, 11:45 AM ET market snapshot
observations.value: NVDA -5.3% after a -14% opening drop; AMD +5.8%, AVGO +5.6%, CRWV -7.2%, MU -3%; S&P 500 +0.1%, Nasdaq roughly flat

observations.label: Catalyst
observations.value: Nvidia confirmed Jensen Huang's departure and Colette Kress as interim CEO; management transition and China-related scrutiny remain company-specific risks

observations.label: Fundamental distinction
observations.value: Custom silicon and alternative accelerators could see stronger interest, but no verified evidence of immediate hyperscaler order reallocations or decreased overall AI chip demand

observations.label: Risks and indicators
observations.value: Relative performance through closing bell, NVDA product/customer commitments and November 17 earnings, AVGO/AMD execution, sector breadth, Treasury yields and financing conditions

items.key_finding: Large intraday outperformance by rival chip suppliers marks a meaningful but not yet sustained semiconductor divergence.

sources.title: MarketWatch / FactSet, late-morning November 12 semiconductor movers
Associated Press, November 12 market swings as of 11:45 a.m. ET

items.title: Nebius revenue surges but capacity delays and higher spending pressure AI-cloud shares
items.summary: Nebius reported third-quarter revenue of $980.8 million, up 571% year over year, but now expects 2026 sales at the low end of its prior range after third-party capacity was delayed. Its spending forecast rose to roughly $27 billion, weighing on premarket shares. Contract retention is encouraging; deployment timing, financing and cash generation remain key risks.

observations.label: Q3 reported November 12
observations.value: Revenue $980.8 million (+571% year-on-year); adjusted EBITDA $465.8 million; net loss from continuing operations $37.5 million

observations.label: 2026 outlook and capacity
observations.value: Revenue expected at low end of $3.0-$3.4 billion; some third-party capacity pushed into H1 2027

observations.label: 2026-2027 capital spending plans
observations.value: 2026 capex around $27 billion versus prior $20-$25 billion; 2027 projected $40-$45 billion, subject to financing and execution

observations.label: Premarket response, November 12
observations.value: Reuters reported NBIS down nearly 12% at 7:16 AM ET; another morning report indicated about -8.3%; both are changing premarket indications

observations.label: What to watch
observations.value: Customer prepayments, contracted capacity delivery dates, funding costs, revised revenue pace and evidence of 2027 pre-tax breakeven

items.key_finding: Exceptional AI cloud demand is not preventing execution delays or a higher capital burden.

sources.title: Reuters November 12 capacity-delay and spending report
